entries.title: OUR BIGGEST ONE THIS SEASON | ASOLUTE MONSTER AT WINKLESPRUIT | LIVE BAIT FISHING
entries.description:
WHAT A SESSION AT WINKLESPRUIT! 🎣🔥

We headed out for another day of fishing and Pa made the perfect call — choosing exactly what to target and where we needed to be.

The decision paid off BIG TIME!

We managed to land two beautiful Garrick, but one of them was on a completely different level. The big fish weighed over 14KG, making it our biggest Garrick of the season so far! 😱🔥

Once Pa hooked into this monster, the real battle began. This fish had plenty of power and wasn't giving up easily. Pa had to follow it for an incredible 2KM down the beach before finally getting the opportunity to land it.

It was an unbelievable fight that showed exactly why experience, patience and knowing how to read the conditions can make such a huge difference.

From choosing the right target, finding the right spot and staying patient throughout the fight — Pa put his experience on display once again.

Two Garrick. One absolute monster. Over 14KG. 2KM of beach. One unforgettable session. 🎣🔥

Pa's Xtreme Fishing does it again! 💪

A massive thank you to everyone who continues to support the channel. We appreciate every single one of you! ❤️

If you enjoyed the video, don't forget to LIKE 👍, COMMENT 💬, SHARE 🔄 and SUBSCRIBE 🔔 for more fishing adventures from the KZN South Coast.

ISIPINGO RIVER MOUTH BREACHES! 🌊 Floodwaters Rush Into the Ocean | Durban Flooding
entries.description:
Heavy rainfall across Durban has caused water levels in the Isipingo River to rise dramatically, prompting an emergency intervention at the Isipingo Beach river mouth.

Following concerns about flooding in surrounding low-lying areas, eThekwini Municipality used machinery to lower and remove sand at the mouth, creating a channel for the accumulated river water to escape into the Indian Ocean.

In this video, I take you right to the Isipingo River mouth to show what is happening. The river is now flowing strongly into the ocean but what makes this footage particularly interesting is watching the breach actively widen. As the water rushes through the opening, it erodes the sandy sides of the channel, causing sections to collapse into the water.

Nearby, the effects of the rising water levels are already clearly visible. A local soccer ground is flooded, while water around the vegetation has risen remarkably high beneath the hanging bird nests.

This footage was captured on 18 September 2026 and documents conditions at the time of filming.

With continued rainfall and flooding affecting parts of Durban, please exercise extreme caution around rivers, flooded roads, low-lying bridges and fast-moving water.

📍 Location: Isipingo Beach, Durban, KwaZulu-Natal
📅 Filmed: 18 September 2026
🎥 Juelz Visuelz

If you enjoy seeing Durban and KwaZulu-Natal from perspectives you don't always get to see, SUBSCRIBE and turn on notifications for more.

entries.title: Durban You Never See | Inside Durban Harbour From Above
entries.description:
There is a side of Durban that most people never get to see.

Captured from above in 2022, this journey begins over the Bluff before moving towards the entrance of Durban Harbour, the Millennium Tower and South Pier.

We then fly deeper into one of South Africa’s most important ports, passing cargo ships, dry-bulk operations, industrial storage tanks and the extensive Island View terminal area.

A full 360-degree aerial view reveals how the harbour, Bluff, Indian Ocean and city all connect. Later, we explore the back of the port around Bayhead and Grunter Gully—an industrial landscape hidden from most residents and visitors.

This is more than a beautiful aerial view. It is a closer look at the working side of Durban and the infrastructure helping connect South Africa to the rest of the world.

Which part of Durban should I explore next? Let me know in the comments.

Please remember to LIKE the video, SUBSCRIBE and turn on notifications for more aerial journeys, local history and hidden places around Durban and KwaZulu-Natal.

entries.description:
#Fishing #durban #Deep Sea Fishing Trip with Saragosa Charters #catchandcook #Rockard #Reds

We took my son out on his very first deep-sea fishing adventure in Durban, and we went with the absolute best in the business—Saragosa Charters. Over the years, these guys have become good friends of ours, and they always deliver an incredible experience!The waters were a bit rough out there, and I’ll admit, the sea sickness got the better of me this time! 🤢 But despite the rocky waves, everyone on the boat had an absolute blast. The crew and the guys kept the energy high and reeled in some amazing catches, including Rockcod, Englishmen, Slingers, Reds, and Stumpies.

After a wild day out on the ocean, we finally made it back home safely. To cap off an unforgettable day, we decided to cook up our fresh catch on my brand-new braai stand that I bought from Temu. I spiced the fish perfectly, wrapped it in foil, and let it slow-cook over the coals. There is nothing better than enjoying a fresh, self-caught meal with the family!A huge shoutout to Saragosa Charters for another memorable trip. Make sure to LIKE, COMMENT, and SUBSCRIBE for more family adventures and fishing trips!

entries.title: Wife’s birthday flowers! #Birthday #Flowers #FreshFlowersOnFlorida #JuelzT
A Garrick He’ll Never Forget! | First ever Garrick for Erza | 12-Year-Old Ezra’s Incredible Story
entries.description:
Some fishing moments are about much more than catching a fish… ❤️🎣

Meet Ezra, an incredible 12-year-old boy who has already faced challenges that no child should ever have to go through. After undergoing several open-heart surgeries, Ezra has shown an unbelievable amount of strength, courage and determination.

Pa had the privilege of taking Ezra fishing, hoping to give him a day he would never forget. And somehow, Ezra gave us a moment that WE will never forget.

🎣 Ezra hooked into an incredible Garrick weighing around 10kg!

Watching him fight that fish, seeing his determination, and then seeing the excitement on Ezra’s face and the faces of his family when he landed it… it was truly something special.

This wasn't just a fishing trip. It was a reminder of how powerful a little happiness, an unforgettable experience and the love of family can be. ❤️

Ezra, you are an absolute inspiration. Your strength and courage are incredible, and we are honoured that Pa’s Xtreme Fishing could be part of this special moment.

We hope this video brings a smile to your face and reminds you that you are capable of amazing things. 💪❤️

🎣 Congratulations, Ezra, on an incredible Garrick!

Thank you to Ezra and his family for allowing us to share this special story with the PXF family.

This one was for Ezra. ❤️🎣

entries.title: Durban Harbour After the Storm | A Lesson to Be Learned
entries.description:
This was the shocking scene inside Durban Harbour on 28 June 2023, after severe weather and heavy rainfall swept across parts of the city.

From a distance, the marina appeared calm. But as the drone moved closer, large sections of the water were almost completely covered by branches, plastic, timber and other waste.

The debris had collected between the boats, against the walkways and throughout the quieter sections of the marina. From directly above, parts of the water appeared almost solid.

This footage shows more than the aftermath of a storm. It reveals how closely connected our streets, drains, rivers, harbour and ocean really are.

The storm did not create all of this waste. It exposed it.

Anything discarded on our streets can be carried into stormwater systems and waterways when heavy rain arrives. What disappears from our neighbourhoods does not disappear from the environment.

Watch until the end and share your thoughts in the comments.

What lesson do you think Durban needs to learn from scenes like these?

Filmed and produced by Juelz Visuelz.

Subscribe for more aerial documentaries, Durban stories, tourism experiences and extraordinary views from across KwaZulu Natal.

Doonside & Warner Beach From Above | The History of Two Coastal Communities
entries.description:
Discover Doonside and Warner Beach from above as we explore the history, coastline and character of these neighbouring communities on the Sapphire Coast of KwaZulu Natal.

Doonside developed around a railway siding that was renamed in 1910 after a nearby house called Lorna Doone. Just beyond the Little Amanzimtoti River, Warner Beach was formally laid out by surveyor P. A. Warner and later developed into a popular seaside holiday village.

From the railway running beside the ocean to the historic hotels, Warner Beach tidal pool, Warnadoone Surf Lifesaving Club and the annual Sardine Run, this coastline has been shaped by tourism, sport and generations of coastal living.

Doonside is known for its quieter beach, river mouth and elevated ocean views, while Warner Beach retains the character of an established surfing and holiday community.

Join me as we experience Doonside and Warner Beach from an entirely different perspective.

Which of these two coastal communities holds the most memories for you? Share your story in the comments.

entries.title: Isipingo Beach Floods 2022 | The Day the Water Took Over
entries.description:
On 12 April 2022, Isipingo Beach was overwhelmed by floodwater after relentless rain across KwaZulu Natal. Roads disappeared beneath muddy water, a playground was submerged and familiar parts of the community became almost unrecognisable.

This original footage documents what happened in Isipingo Beach during the devastating April 2022 KZN floods.

On 11 and 12 April, parts of KwaZulu Natal received between 200 and 400 mm of rain within just 24 hours. The entire eThekwini metro was among the areas most severely affected.

By 18 April 2022, official figures recorded 443 people dead in KwaZulu Natal, approximately 48 missing or unaccounted for, more than 40 000 displaced, nearly 4 000 homes completely destroyed and over 8 300 partially damaged.

In Isipingo, local reports described homes near Isipingo Beach completely flooded and boats being used to rescue workers trapped in shoulder high water.

This video is more than dramatic footage. It is a visual record of a disaster that changed communities across KZN. We remember those who lost their lives, homes and livelihoods.

Were you in Isipingo Beach or elsewhere in KZN during the floods? Share what you witnessed in the comments.

Original footage and photography: Juelz T

Information sources: South African Government, World Meteorological Organization and The Witness.

entries.title: Scottburgh Beach Fishing | Shad and Big Blacktail Caught
entries.description:
I spent a beautiful morning at Scottburgh Beach on the KwaZulu Natal South Coast, where a number of anglers were fishing from the rocks.

I did not do much fishing myself, but I took out the camera and captured some of the action. A few shad were caught, along with some seriously impressive blacktail.

Scottburgh Rock is a fantastic place to cast a line, enjoy the ocean and experience the beauty of the KZN coastline.

If you enjoy fishing, outdoor adventures and videos showcasing beautiful places around South Africa, please like this video, share it with your fellow anglers and subscribe to Juelz T for more.

Let me know in the comments:

What is the biggest blacktail you have ever caught?

Location: Scottburgh Beach, KwaZulu Natal, South Africa

#ScottburghBeach #FishingSouthAfrica #KZNFishing #JuelzT

entries.title: https://youtu.be/VE8S9LUFqeI?si=x7Usz0APp_SHSUq_
Monster Garrick at Winklespruit | KZN South Coast | 4 MASSIVE Garrick caught | Live bait fishing
entries.description:
Pa and the team headed down to Winklespruit this past week in search of some monster Garrick — and guess what? They found exactly what they were looking for! 

The team managed to land 4 beautiful Garrick, with the biggest weighing an incredible 13kg. We used live Shad as bait and slid them out using braid and line.

It turned out to be an amazing morning of fishing, with plenty of action and some serious fish!

To make it even more special, Pa gave his cameraman Trev the opportunity to fight and land a beautiful Garrick of his own. It was Trev’s first time fighting a fish of this size, and what an experience it was!

Another fantastic day on the water with Pa and the team.
